ocsf_class.format: The class_name caption; class_uid is the same fact as a number and is not separately tabled here.

API Activity.meaning: A CloudTrail or EKS control-plane API call.

Network Activity.meaning: A VPC Flow Logs connection record.

HTTP Activity.meaning: An AWS WAF web ACL inspection of one HTTP request.

DNS Activity.meaning: A Route 53 Resolver query log entry.

Detection Finding.meaning: A Security Hub finding from a detective control such as GuardDuty.

Compliance Finding.meaning: A Security Hub finding from a compliance standard check.

Vulnerability Finding.meaning: A Security Hub finding from Amazon Inspector.

ocsf_category.format: The category_name caption; category_uid is the same fact as a number and is not separately tabled here.

ocsf_type_tag.format: Derived, not independently set: type_uid = class_uid * 100 + activity_id; type_name is class_name joined to activity_name with a colon.

severity.format: A fixed 8-value scale from Unknown/Other through Fatal (severity_id, severity); the caption is tabled here, the numeric id is the same fact as a number.

Low.meaning: The reader decides if action is needed.

Medium.meaning: Action is required but the situation is not urgent.

Critical.meaning: Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.

Fatal.meaning: An error occurred too late for remedial action.

Other.meaning: Not mapped to the scale; see the caption.

event_status.format: Success, Failure, Unknown or Other (status_id, status); captions only.

action.format: Unknown, Allowed, Denied or Other (action_id, action); captions only, the numeric id is the same fact as a number.

disposition.format: Up to 29 captions (disposition_id, disposition); only the ones this family's samples and vendor pages use are enumerated, captions only.

Alert.meaning: Flagged as a threat but not blocked.

Count.meaning: Counted only; no allow/block decision made.

observable_name.format: A dotted attribute path within this record, or a literal like answers[].rdata for a repeated field.

observable_type.format: A fixed OCSF vocabulary of pivotable value kinds (type_id, type), 23 values; captions only, the numeric id is the same fact as a number.

Resource UID.meaning: A cloud resource's unique id, for example an S3 bucket name or EC2 instance id.

observable_value.format: Whatever the pointed-at attribute holds; same value, duplicated here for a flat pivot table.

cloud_provider.format: A fixed word naming the vendor.

cloud_region.format: An AWS Region code such as us-east-1.

cloud_account_id.format: A 12-digit AWS account id. Sample account ids in this family are AWS's own doc placeholders, not real accounts.

cloud_zone.format: An AZ id such as use1-az1.

metadata_product_name.format: A fixed per-source string: CloudTrail, Amazon EKS, Route 53, Amazon VPC, AWS WAF, or the Security Hub finding's own ProductName.

metadata_product_feature.format: A fixed per-source string, e.g. Resolver Query Logs, Flowlogs, Management, Elastic Kubernetes Service.

metadata_product_version.format: A version string; shape varies by product (semantic, date-based or a bare integer).

metadata_log_version.format: A version string from the original log, not OCSF's own.

endpoint_instance_uid.format: An i-... EC2 instance id or an rslvr-in-... Resolver inbound endpoint id.

endpoint_svc_name.format: A service name such as ALB, or - when not applicable.

endpoint_uid.format: A resource id string whose shape depends on which service fronted the request.

connection_direction.format: Unknown, Inbound, Outbound, Lateral or Other (direction_id, direction); captions only.

Lateral.meaning: Traffic between peers at the same boundary.

connection_protocol_num.format: An integer, e.g. 6 for TCP, 17 for UDP.

connection_boundary.format: One of 13 boundary captions (boundary_id, boundary); captions only.

Localhost.meaning: Local network traffic on the same endpoint.

Internal.meaning: Internal network traffic between two endpoints inside the network.

External.meaning: External network traffic between two endpoints on the internet or outside the network.

Same VPC.meaning: Through another resource in the same VPC.

Internet/VPC Gateway.meaning: Through an internet gateway or a gateway VPC endpoint.

Intra-region VPC.meaning: Through an intra-region VPC peering connection.

Inter-region VPC.meaning: Through an inter-region VPC peering connection.

Gateway VPC.meaning: Through a gateway VPC endpoint (Nitro-based instances only).

Internet Gateway.meaning: Through an internet gateway (Nitro-based instances only).

Other.meaning: The boundary is not mapped; see the caption.

connection_tcp_flags.format: A bitmask: FIN=1, SYN=2, RST=4, SYN-ACK=18. Flags OR together within the aggregation window, so 19 means SYN-ACK and FIN both occurred.
connection_tcp_flags.quote: If no supported flags are recorded, the TCP flag value is 0.

start_time.format: An epoch-ms integer (start_time) with an ISO companion (start_time_dt).

end_time.format: An ISO-8601 companion timestamp (end_time_dt); VPC Flow Logs in this family did not carry a matching epoch-ms end_time.

flow_status_code.format: One of three log-status captions, carried into OCSF's status_code attribute.

NODATA.meaning: No traffic to or from the interface during the window.

SKIPDATA.meaning: Some records were skipped, from an internal capacity limit or error.

firewall_rule_uid.format: A rule id; Default_Action when no configured rule matched and the web ACL's default action applied.

activity_api.format: Create, Read, Update, Delete, Unknown or Other (activity_id, activity_name); captions only.

activity_network.format: Open, Close, Reset, Fail, Refuse, Traffic, Unknown or Other (activity_id, activity_name); captions only.

Reset.meaning: The connection was abnormally terminated, e.g. by a firewall.

Fail.meaning: The connection failed, e.g. timeout or no route.

Refuse.meaning: The connection was refused, e.g. closed port.

Traffic.meaning: A traffic volume report, not a lifecycle event.

activity_http.format: One of the 8 standard HTTP methods, Unknown or Other (activity_id, activity_name); captions only.

Post.meaning: POST: submit an entity, often a state change.

activity_dns.format: Query, Traffic, Unknown or Other (activity_id, activity_name); captions only.

activity_finding.format: Create, Update, Close, Unknown or Other (activity_id, activity_name); captions only.

api_operation.format: The service's own operation name, not normalized to a fixed set.

api_response_data.format: A JSON string, not parsed further by OCSF.

http_user_agent.format: A free-text client identification string, e.g. an SDK/OS/runtime signature or a browser UA.

actor_user_uid_alt.format: An IAM unique id (AIDA.../AROA.../AKIA... prefix family).

actor_credential_uid.format: An AKIA... long-term access key id, or an ASIA... temporary session credential id.

actor_user_type.format: A vendor-defined caption (CloudTrail's identity type string) or a numeric type_id (EKS audit, from the Kubernetes user info); both bound here where each sourcetype carries one or the other. This family's cloudtrail sample carries only IAMUser; CloudTrail's own userIdentity.type also uses Root, AssumedRole, FederatedUser, Role, SAMLUser and others, documented on the reference aws-cloudtrail pack, not repeated here. CloudTrail's identity type also uses Root, AssumedRole, FederatedUser, Role, SAMLUser; documented on the aws-cloudtrail pack.

IAMUser.meaning: An IAM user's own long-term credentials.

examples.note: AWS's own EXAMPLE-convention placeholder, 13 digits as published

actor_session_uid.format: A session id string from the Kubernetes user info extra fields.

actor_user_groups.format: One or more Kubernetes group names.

resources_namespace.format: A namespace name, or absent for cluster-scoped kinds.

resources_version.format: A Kubernetes apiVersion string, e.g. v1.

query_hostname.format: A fully-qualified domain name, trailing dot included as Resolver logs it.

query_type.format: An IANA DNS RR type mnemonic. Reused for both query.type and answers[].type, the same vocabulary.

IN.meaning: Internet class, the only one in ordinary use.

dns_answer_rdata.format: The RDATA for the answer's type; an IP literal for A/AAAA.

rcode.format: An RFC 6895 DNS response code (rcode_id, rcode); captions only.

NXDomain.meaning: The queried domain does not exist.

NotAuth.meaning: Not authorized or not authoritative for the zone.

dns_firewall_domain_list_id.format: An rslvr-fdl-... id. Seen only in the unmapped bucket of the sample; not confirmed against a fetched DNS Firewall field reference page.

vpcflow_sublocation_type.format: wavelength, outpost or localzone; a dash when the traffic is not from a sublocation.

vpcflow_sublocation_id.format: A sublocation id; a dash when not applicable.

http_method.format: A standard HTTP method verb; AWS WAF's own field list does not further enumerate it, so no full table is claimed.

http_request_uid.format: A trace id or request id, shape depends on the fronting service.
http_request_uid.quote: For Application Load Balancer, this is the trace ID. For all others, this is the request ID.

http_request_args.format: The raw query string, empty when there is none.

http_status.format: A standard HTTP status code; null when the request was blocked before a response existed.

ja4_fingerprint.quote: The JA4 fingerprint is a 36-character hash derived from the TLS Client Hello of an incoming request.

firewall_rule_type.format: One of AWS WAF's terminatingRuleType captions.

MANAGED_RULE_GROUP.meaning: An AWS or Marketplace managed rule group.

firewall_rule_type.quote: Possible values: RATE_BASED, REGULAR, GROUP, and MANAGED_RULE_GROUP.

firewall_rule_condition.quote: The rule trigger condition for the rule. For example: SQL_INJECTION.

firewall_rule_match_location.format: A request component name, e.g. HEADER.
firewall_rule_match_location.quote: The location of the matched data in the source which resulted in the triggered firewall rule. For example: HEADER.

firewall_rule_match_details.quote: The data in a request that rule matched. For example: '["10","and","1"]'.

firewall_rule_sensitivity.format: A level word. Seen in the sample; not confirmed against a fetched AWS WAF rule-statement sensitivity reference page, so left documented-free.

waf_rule_group_id.format: A rule group id, often an AWS-managed group name such as AWS#AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet.
waf_rule_group_id.quote: The ID of the rule group.

waf_http_fragment.quote: The part of a URL that follows the "#" symbol, providing additional information about the resource.

compliance_control.format: A control id or short name.
compliance_control.quote: A Control is prescriptive, prioritized, and simplified set of best practices that one can use to strengthen their cybersecurity posture.

compliance_requirements.quote: A list of requirements associated to a specific control in an industry or regulatory framework.

compliance_standards.quote: Security standards are a set of criteria organizations can follow to protect sensitive and confidential information.

finding_status.format: New, In Progress, Suppressed, Resolved, Unknown or Other (status_id, status); captions only.

Suppressed.meaning: Reviewed and judged benign or a false positive.

finding_status.quote: The resultant status of the compliance check normalized to the caption of the status_id value.

evidence_data.format: A JSON object whose shape depends on the evidence's own source.
evidence_data.quote: Describes various evidence artifacts associated to the activity/activities that triggered a security detection.

finding_uid.format: An id string, shape depends on the finding provider (GuardDuty, Inspector, a control check).

finding_title.quote: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the reported finding.

finding_types.format: One or more slash-delimited taxonomy strings.

finding_src_url.quote: The URL pointing to the source of the finding.

finding_first_seen_time.quote: It can differ from the created_time timestamp, which reflects the time this finding was created.

remediation_desc.quote: The description of the remediation strategy.

finding_resource_type.format: An AWS CloudFormation-style resource type name.

cve_cvss_vector.format: A CVSS vector string, e.g. AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N.

vuln_is_exploit_available.quote: Indicates if an exploit or a PoC (proof-of-concept) is available for the reported vulnerability.

vuln_is_fix_available.quote: Indicates if a fix is available for the reported vulnerability.

pkg_epoch.format: A small integer as a string.

ACTIVE.meaning: The finding is current and visible by default.

ARCHIVED.meaning: The finding is hidden from the default view but not deleted.

securityhub_record_state.quote: By default, when initially generated by a service, findings are considered ACTIVE.

securityhub_workflow_state.format: A workflow status word such as NEW; the field itself is retired in favor of the Workflow object.
securityhub_workflow_state.quote: This object is retired and has been replaced by the Status field of the Workflow object.

securityhub_sample.quote: Specifies whether the finding is a sample finding.

record_time.format: An epoch-ms integer (time) with an ISO-8601 companion (time_dt); the same instant, two encodings.

metadata_event_code.format: A fixed word; the aws-cloudtrail reference pack's event_type concept documents the full vocabulary (AwsApiCall, AwsServiceEvent, AwsConsoleSignIn and others).

http_header.format: A header name (http_headers[].name) or its value (http_headers[].value); both bound here.

http_referrer.format: A URL, or null when the client sent no Referer header.
